summary.text: Jeff Merkley is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election to the U.S. Senate from Oregon, where he has served since January 2009. A Stanford and Princeton graduate who worked on defense policy and then in affordable housing, he served in the Oregon House from 1999 to 2009, the last two years as Speaker. His Senate office says he is focused on health care, housing, education and good-paying jobs.

paragraphs.text: Merkley was born in Myrtle Creek, Oregon, where his father worked as a millwright; according to his Senate office, the family later moved to Roseburg and then to East Multnomah County. In 1979 he became the first person in his family to graduate from college, earning a bachelor's degree from Stanford University, and he later earned a master's degree from Princeton University in 1982.
After an internship in the office of Sen. Mark Hatfield, he worked in Washington, D.C., on nuclear disarmament and military spending.
He then returned to Oregon, volunteered with Habitat for Humanity, became executive director of Portland Area Habitat and afterward developed affordable housing for another nonprofit.

Merkley ran for the state legislature in 1998 and was elected to represent the East Multnomah County neighborhood where he grew up, serving in the Oregon House from 1999 until his election to the Senate in 2008. He was elected Speaker in 2007.
In the Senate he holds the seat once held by Hatfield, and he won re-election in 2014 and 2020.

Merkley sits on the Appropriations, Environment and Public Works, Budget, Rules and Foreign Relations committees, chairs the Appropriations subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies and an Environment and Public Works subcommittee, and co-chairs the Congressional-Executive Commission on China.
According to his Senate office, he holds a town hall in each of Oregon's 36 counties every year. He and his wife, Mary Sorteberg, have two children and live in East Portland.
